summary.oneLiner: Amal Ltd manufactures bulk chemicals — Sulphuric acid, Oleum and their downstream products (Sulphur dioxide, Sulphur trioxide) — at its Ankleshwar site, serving customers largely within a 200 km radius.
summary.business: The Company manufactures bulk chemicals such as Sulphuric acid, Oleum and their downstream products such as Sulphur dioxide and Sulphur trioxide at its manufacturing site in Ankleshwar. These chemicals are used in several industries, such as Dyestuffs, Fertilisers, Personal Care, Petrochemicals, Pharmaceuticals and Textiles, and the products are generally sold within a 200 km radius of the manufacturing site. Its wholly-owned material subsidiary, Amal Speciality Chemicals Ltd, operates a second manufacturing facility making the same product family.

risks.risk: Majority of group scale sits inside an unlisted material subsidiary
risks.note: Standalone revenue (Rs 8,491 lakh) is materially smaller than consolidated revenue (Rs 23,964 lakh), indicating a large majority of the Group's scale resides in Amal Speciality Chemicals Ltd, an unlisted 'material subsidiary'. The Audit Committee's charter separately calls out reviewing 'significant transactions and arrangements entered into by the unlisted subsidiary company' and 'investments made by an unlisted subsidiary company', reflecting the governance/disclosure complexity of running most of the business through an unlisted entity.

risks.risk: Key management and board leadership overlap with the promoter/holding-company group
risks.note: The Managing Director's remuneration is explicitly computed with reference to (and paid in coordination with) Atul Ltd, the holding company, of which he is an employee; the Chairman (a promoter, Non-executive Director) is also Chairman and Managing Director of Atul Ltd; and another Non-executive Director is also an Executive Director/CFO of Atul Ltd. This concentration of leadership roles with the holding company creates dependency on and potential conflicts of interest with the promoter group.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The world market for Sulphuric acid is estimated at about 310 million tonnes per annum and the Indian market at about 18.5 million tonnes per annum; both markets are growing at about 3% per annum.
- Success in this business depends on ensuring high capacity utilisation, excellent conversion efficiency and full deployment of the steam.
- The products manufactured by the Company are commodities in nature whose prices and contribution margins fluctuate significantly.
- Revenue growth during the year was driven by an unprecedented spike in the price of Sulphur, the Company's main raw material, attributed to constrained production, geopolitical disruptions and a significant rise in nickel refining and fertiliser production; volume growth was comparatively modest.
- The facility at Amal Speciality Chemicals has stabilised operations.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Two main business mandates: first, to further improve existing operations; second, to articulate projects to grow beyond the current level of operations.
- A third mandate is people development, to build an internal pipeline of leadership.
- Optimising the product mix remains a key growth factor.
- The Company remains committed to strengthening its foundations and seeking sustainable (ESG + Economic) growth to create enduring value for stakeholders.
- The Company states it is committed to the efficient utilisation of monetary resources generated from operations to deliver long-term sustainable growth and enhance value for stakeholders. Net borrowings are stated as nil. Dividend is identified as a key interest/concern of shareholders, engaged with on an ongoing basis through the Annual General Meeting, Annual Report and stock exchange filings.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: CapEx related to upgradation of the Sulphur yard was completed in 2025-26. Three CapEx projects are currently under implementation: (1) increasing sales of steam, a co-product; (2) automation in the old plant to further improve monitoring of process parameters and increase people productivity; and (3) upgrading canteen facilities. Separately, the Company is evaluating two growth projects and will decide the next steps while keeping in focus the external business environment. The facility at the material subsidiary, Amal Speciality Chemicals, has stabilised operations.
